label: Player characters: one fixed sprite per race, role and gender, hands empty (held weapons are drawn over the sprite by player-held-weapon-overlay.ts). Prototypes.
style: Hand-painted dark-fantasy game character, painterly and believable in its materials, but designed above all as a bold, iconic game piece that reads at 48 pixels: large, simple masses of saturated colour, very few small details, clear light and dark separation between head, torso, legs and gear, the role's signature clothing and armour unmistakable. Warm key light from the upper left and a cool rim light along the right edges.

rules.item: One full-body figure. Image 1 is the pixel-art sprite this art replaces: keep its stance and leg position, but the figure always faces the right side of the picture: a three-quarter view with the body, the head and the eyes all turned toward the viewer's right; the nose points to the right side of the picture. Never turn the head or the body to the left. Use stylized, chunky game proportions: a big head about one quarter of the height, a sturdy body, big hands and feet. Both hands are completely empty: the arms hang relaxed and slightly away from the body, hands at hip height, fingers loosely curled as if about to grip a handle. Nothing is held or carried in the hands, and there are no weapons anywhere: no sword, axe, shield, staff, whip, tool, sheathed or slung blade, and no magic effects; ignore the weapons in image 1, because the game draws them on top separately. Paint it as hand-painted art and ignore the blocky pixels. Fully transparent background: no ground, no cast shadow, no text, no frame.
